title: The gap is stated as a representational impossibility when the evidence shows a search-range convention
quote: None of these can represent, much less estimate, a negative confidence--correctness association.
explanation: The empirical half of the gap is genuinely demonstrated: Table I and results/tact_eval.json confirm CISC-devT and the ECE gate sit exactly at the SC floor for every kappa < 0, and fixed-gamma CISC collapses to 0.000 at gamma in {2,4}. The diagnosis is one level too strong. 'Cannot represent' is a claim about expressive capacity; what is shown is that published protocols instantiate their grids on non-negative exponents, which the paper's own baseline description confirms ('positive grid picked on dev'). SignGrid-dev is the same weight family with the sign released and it reaches the signed oracle across the whole negative half-axis. The barrier is one sign bit in a hyperparameter range. The universals 'Every published weighting scheme' and 'None of these' also carry no search scope, venue range, or date range, and the single hedge 'to the author's knowledge' is dropped in both the abstract and Related Work.

title: The abstract names the weaker of the two designated killer baselines and drops the stronger one
quote: pin every published protocol to the majority-vote floor ($\kappa=-0.6$: $1.000$ vs.\ $0.807$)
explanation: The delta a reader infers from this sentence is 0.193 over the published floor. In that same cell SignGrid-dev also scores 1.000, and results/tact_eval.json records TACT-dev_vs_SignGrid there as {a_only: 0, b_only: 0, p_value: 1.0}: bit-identical decisions. Across the nine sweep cells SignGrid-dev ties TACT-dev five times and is strictly ahead four times, never behind. The abstract's falsifier sentence names only CISC-devT as the designated killer and omits the signed grid, which is the comparator that actually constrains the contribution. On this axis the honest delta over the paper's own trivial baseline is 0.000, and the contribution is the label-free estimate of the sign rather than the recovery itself. Saying so costs one clause and is the difference between a reviewer finding the concession and the author making it.

title: Related Work is a citation ledger: 20 of 26 references in 272 words, four with no characterization
quote: Weighted variants \cite{li2023diverse,borda2025} and early-stopping families \cite{aggarwal2023adaptive,li2024escape} refine the budget
explanation: Nine keys sit in the first paragraph, six in one sentence of the second, four in one sentence of the third. li2023diverse, borda2025, aggarwal2023adaptive and li2024escape receive no characterization at all, and borda2025 is the one rank-based aggregator in the list, filed as a budget mechanism. fuse2026 and beyondmajority2025 are the two closest published neighbours to C2, label-free aggregation beyond majority voting, and are separated from it by a single unevidenced clause. No paragraph states what the field collectively believes and where that belief breaks, which is what a related-work section is for.

title: The remedy for the paper's worst failure mode sits uncited in its own bibliography
quote:
a dominant
wrong cluster that is semantically tight but carries no verbatim signature, so
deduplication has nothing to collapse
explanation: The unguarded failure follows from deduplication being purely lexical. kuhn2023semantic, semantic-equivalence clustering, is the standard published response and appears as an uncited bibitem in this very paper. Calling the mode 'unguarded' without noting that a guard exists in the literature overstates how fundamental the limitation is.
